item.title: Trump rallies New York crowd for Republican Bruce Blakeman's bid to replace Gov. Kathy Hochul
item.description: President Donald Trump rallied Syracuse supporters behind Bruce Blakeman's bid to unseat Gov. Kathy Hochul, promising tax cuts and cheaper energy for New York families.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump returned to his home state of New York on Friday night, showcasing America's "New Golden Age" and promising to help Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman flip the Empire State red as the GOP makes its final push toward November's midterm elections.

Trump rallied supporters in Syracuse with a sweeping celebration of his administration's economic and immigration agenda, pledging to help New Yorkers secure lower taxes, cheaper energy and safer streets by electing Republicans up and down the ballot.

"We're in the Golden Age of America," Trump told the crowd, urging supporters to deliver the same enthusiasm that powered his presidential campaigns.

TRUMP CAMPAIGN INSIDER REVEALS STRATEGY BEHIND MIDTERM BLITZ THAT WHITE HOUSE HOPES PAYS OFF BIG

"Please pretend I'm on the freaking ballot," Trump urged. "And in a really, in a certain way, I am on the ballot because they can take away everything that we, that we got."

The president took Blakeman's challenge to Democrat Gov. Kathy Hochul as the centerpiece of the rally, promising direct support from Washington if elected.

"[Blakeman will] save this state. He'll turn the state around and I'll help him from the White House," Trump said. "I'll be helping him for governor."

Trump blasted Hochul over New York's taxes, utility bills and public safety, arguing that Blakeman could unleash the state's economic potential by embracing domestic energy production and cutting costs for families.

DEBRA MESSING SAYS COST OF LIVING, SUBWAY VIOLENCE PUSHED HER TO BACK TRUMP-ENDORSED REPUBLICAN

The president also hailed his administration's economic agenda as proof of what Trump described as a remarkable national turnaround.

He singled out Micron's planned $100 billion semiconductor complex in central New York, a project the company says is expected to generate 50,000 jobs across the state, including 9,000 directly with Micron.

"This will soon be the home to the largest semiconductor manufacturing facility ever built in the Western Hemisphere," Trump said.

Blakeman joined Trump onstage and echoed the president's message of a Republican resurgence, promising to cut taxes and utility bills, focus on public safety and make New York more attractive to both businesses and families.

"We have to create good jobs, good benefits to keep our young people here," Blakeman said. "We gotta look at business not as the enemy, but as a partner."

Trump also threw his support behind Republican congressional candidates Kailee Buller, who is challenging Democrat Rep. John Mannion in New York's 22nd District, and Anthony Constantino, who is running for the state's open 21st District seat, pledging to help Republicans compete for both seats.

The rally also notably featured a brief but memorable on-stage appearance by legendary former heavyweight boxing champion Mike Tyson, whom Trump invited up before the crowd.

"I'm just happy to be up here with my president, President Trump," Tyson said. "And, there's no way in the world I would ever be here if it wasn't for a president like Donald Trump. Thank you. Thank you very much."

Trump responded with a laugh, recalling Tyson's notorious reputation.

"I don't want to fight him," Trump joked, before complimenting the former champion. "You look good. Mike. What the h— are you doing?"

With Election Day approaching, the president returned to his core message that Republicans need Trump supporters to make a roaring showing at the ballot box.

"We're going to elect a Republican House and Republican Senate," Trump said.

item.title: An NYC Curse: Rangers top goalie dragged off ice as New York sports nightmare deepens
item.description: Igor Shesterkin jammed his right leg against the post during a net-mouth scramble and had to be helped off the ice by New York Rangers teammates.
item.content:encoded:
The New York Rangers could be in a tough spot after star goaltender Igor Shesterkin exited Friday night's game with what appeared to be a lower-body injury and needed to be helped off the ice.

The Rangers have been off to a hot start this season and came into Friday night's game against the Washington Capitals leading the Eastern Conference.

The 2021-22 Vezina Trophy winner came into the night with a 3-1 record on the year along with a solid .926 save percentage and 1.75 goals against average.

As if that wasn't good enough, he also scored a goal back on Oct. 1.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

But in the second period on Friday night, with the game tied at 1-1, Shesterkin found himself way out of position during a net-mouth scramble. He slid across the crease to the far post, but appeared to jam his right leg awkwardly against the post.

Shesterkin was clearly in a lot of pain and needed to be helped off the ice by his teammates. It looked like he was unable to put weight on his right leg.

It was confirmed later in the game that he would not return.

NHL TEAM AVOIDS NIGHTMARE SCENARIO AS COACH REVEALS LATEST ON STAR CAPTAIN AFTER TERRIFYING INJURY SCARE

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Dylan Garand entered the game in relief, but had only four NHL games on his resume.

If you're a hockey fan, you know that losing Shesterkin for any period of time is a big problem for the Blueshirts.

If you're not a hockey fan, just look at Rangers fans' faces when Shesterkin went down.

The team will be hoping it's not as bad as it looked, but it did start a discussion on social media: did the New York Knicks curse the rest of the city's teams?

Because since the Knicks won an NBA title, injuries have befallen Yankees star Aaron Judge and Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart.

Now, they could be adding Shesterkin to that list of key players who went down with injury.

Of course, they'll take it one step at a time, and while Garand played pretty well after coming into the game, Boone Jenner was able to sneak one past him late in the second, and that proved to be the game-winner.

item.title: Trump brings Mike Tyson on stage at Syracuse rally, jokes that he is Bruce Blakeman's personal security
item.description: Trump brought Mike Tyson on Air Force One to a Syracuse rally for Bruce Blakeman, the Republican running to unseat New York Gov. Kathy Hochul.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump was in his home state of New York, this time in Syracuse, to campaign for Bruce Blakeman, the Republican candidate for the state's gubernatorial election.

Trump though had a special guest in Mike Tyson, who visited the White House earlier in the day and took the trip to Syracuse on Air Force One alongside Trump.

While Trump was campaigning for Blakeman, he shouted Tyson and his physical stature out.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"I see somebody in the audience that I will never fight, I promise. But I remember when Mike [Tyson] was in his prime, when he was the heavyweight champion of the world. He’d stand in the corner and his people would all be holding him back. He wanted to kill whoever it was," Trump said. He was a very dangerous person actually, and he was one of the greatest fighters in history."

Trump then cracked a joke that Tyson was there to protect Blakeman.

"I see him standing right next to Bruce Blakeman. Bruce wants a little protection, he’s got the right guy. Bruce knows who to stand near," Trump said.

Later on, Tyson was called up on stage.

TRUMP GIVES RAW REACTION AFTER FINDING OUT ABOUT MIKE DITKA'S DEATH: 'A TOUGH COOKIE'

"Thank you very much. I'm just happy to be here with my president, President Trump, and there's no way in the world I would ever be here if it wasn't for a president like Donald Trump. Thank you," Tyson said.

"I watched him get in the ring many times. He was a scary guy. I think he looks better now than he did 30 years ago," Trump said when Tyson left the stage. "What the hell are you doing, Mike?"

Trump and Tyson were also joined by New York Yankees president Randy Levine, two days after the Bombers were swept in the American League Division Series. Trump made mention of the postseason loss, but joked that it didn't matter, because "he's won so much, it's not going to matter."

Blakeman will be vying to take Kathy Hochul out of office. Hochul has been the state's governor since August 2021.

Trump made the trip before he was originally slated to attend Saturday's Alabama-Georgia game in Tuscaloosa, but Hurricane Isaias ruined those plans, the White House announced Friday.

item.title: Gov Kathy Hochul signs New York onto Trump's school choice program despite teachers union opposition
item.description: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul joined President Donald Trump's Education Freedom Tax Credit despite fierce opposition from teachers unions and a petition to reject it.
item.content:encoded:
New York Gov. Kathy Hochul on Friday signed on to join President Donald Trump’s school choice program despite opposition from teachers unions.

"Every parent wants their child to have a great education and the best possible chance to succeed. That’s what guides my decisions as governor," Hochul announced Friday.

"New York’s public schools are the backbone of communities across this state," she added. "That’s why I’ve made historic investments in public education, increasing school funding by more than $10 billion and fully funding Foundation Aid for the first time."

GOV HOCHUL'S PLAN TO OPT NEW YORK INTO FEDERAL SCHOOL CHOICE PROGRAM DRAWS UNION OPPOSITION

Despite Hochul's stated intention to participate, major labor groups and teachers unions remain staunchly opposed. A coalition of teachers unions and other public school advocates launched a petition demanding that Hochul reject the program.

"Gov. Hochul plans to opt New York in starting in 2027. But most New Yorkers haven’t even heard of this program or know how it will affect New York," the petition states. "Tax dollars would help pay private tuition for families who never used public schools."

Sydney Altfield, Scholarships for All founder and Teach Coalition CEO, told Fox News Digital, "This is a tremendous day for New Yorkers. Millions of children across our state will now have access to scholarships that can help pay for tutoring, after-school programs and other educational needs.

"Gov. Hochul has kept her promise to New York families, helping put money back into the pockets of hardworking parents while expanding educational opportunities for children across the state."

PRO-TRUMP GROUP LEADS NEW COALITION TO UNDERCUT TEACHERS UNIONS

Hochul’s announcement came after the Department of the Treasury and the IRS issued proposed regulations Oct. 1 to implement the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit (FSTC) program, paving the way for America's first nationwide school choice framework.

The initiative, also referred to as the Education Freedom Tax Credit, allows individual taxpayers to receive up to a $1,700 dollar-for-dollar federal tax credit for donations made to non-profit scholarship-granting organizations (SGOs). However, state governors must formally opt into the program for their residents and local educational organizations to participate and receive the funds.

The IRS recently reported that more than half of U.S. states have already signed up to participate. Burke noted that "competitive pressure" will ultimately force blue states to capture the influx of private donations.

Education Secretary Linda McMahon previously noted that some Democratic leaders have resisted the federal scholarship program simply because "it’s a Trump measure."

Democratic governors who have traditionally opposed school choice initiatives will face mounting competitive pressure to join Trump's program as states weigh whether to participate and Hochul moves to formally opt in, a top Department of Education official told Fox News Digital.

Kentucky has since formally joined the federal program after the state legislature overrode Gov. Andy Beshear's veto of opt-in legislation.

Unlike traditional voucher programs that draw directly from municipal or state public education funds, tax credit scholarships allow taxpayers to redirect a portion of their federal tax liability toward non-profit funding for student scholarships. The federal framework leaves the opt-in decision to state governors, enabling local families to access federally incentivized scholarship dollars.

"I’ve been clear from the start that New York would participate in the federal scholarship tax credit program if, and only if, all schools and students, including those in our public schools, could benefit," Hochul said.

"After a careful review of the federal regulations, we believe this program has the potential to bring millions of additional dollars to New York students and families without taking a single dollar from public schools or our state or local budgets.

"I’m not going to leave money on the table when it could help our kids," she added. "That’s why I have also been directly engaging with business leaders who have committed to use this program to support public school students and their academic needs. 

"I look forward to working with education leaders across the state to make sure these resources reach students in every community. My commitment to public education has not changed, and it never will."

MORE THAN 400K NEW YORK CITY CHILDREN ENROLLED IN FAILING PUBLIC SCHOOLS: REPORT

For decades, school choice initiatives have remained a third-rail issue for many Democrats, who contend that choice models weaken public school systems and undermine labor unions. 

However, growing parent demand for alternative education options — including charter schools, private schooling and homeschooling after the COVID-19 pandemic — has pushed several prominent Democrats to reevaluate their positions.

Trump's landmark school choice program comes as major blue city school districts struggle to retain students since the coronavirus pandemic.

item.title: Lions head coach pays tribute to Mike Ditka after learning of his death from a press conference question
item.description: Dan Campbell shared an unforgettable pre-draft story about sitting alone with Mike Ditka in a room full of cigar smoke ahead of the 1999 NFL Draft.
item.content:encoded:
Reactions are pouring in after news broke of the death of legendary NFL coach Mike Ditka, and one of the best came from Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell.

The Lions coach was in the midst of a news conference when a reporter asked if he had heard the news of Ditka's passing at the age of 86.

He hadn't, and that led to Campbell telling the story of his experience with Ditka ahead of the 1999 NFL Draft.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Campbell was a tight end out of Texas A&M heading into the draft, and like any prospect, he did some interviews with teams.

One of those teams was the New Orleans Saints, who were coached at the time by Ditka, who was also a tight end in his playing days.

"[Ditka] was someone I loved, man. Growing up, Ditka was it," Campbell said. "[I'm a] huge fan."

He said that the Saints, and specifically Ditka, wanted to meet with him.

While Campbell knew the legendary coach would be in the room, he thought others would be in there too.

Nope.

Just him, Ditka, and a room full of cigar smoke.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"It was one of the best times of my life and most intimidating times of my life sitting across from Mike Ditka," Campbell said. "It was awesome, man. Him asking questions about where you grew up, how you think, how you're wired, the game, what you see, it was awesome.

"Thoughts and prayers go out to his family. He's a legend."

What a classy tribute, and to pull that story out of his hat in the moment shows just how much the late coach meant to Campbell.

Of course, the Saints did not end up drafting Campbell. Instead, he was selected by the New York Giants in the third round, 79th overall.

item.title: James Talarico resurfaces after extended absence as his campaign pushes back
item.description: James Talarico resurfaces at Austin City Limits after a 12-day absence that drew sharp attacks from Trump and Ken Paxton on the campaign trail.
item.content:encoded:
Texas Democratic U.S. Senate nominee James Talarico reappeared on the campaign trail Friday after a nearly two-week absence, ending days of speculation and criticism from political opponents regarding his whereabouts.

"Hate to disappoint the conspiracy theorists, but James is still alive and meeting with voters at ACL today," Talarico’s primary spokesperson, JT Ennis, wrote on X.

The post included a video of the candidate walking through crowds and greeting supporters at the Austin City Limits Music Festival.

MEET THE VOTERS WHO COULD BREAK THE GOP’S DECADESLONG GRIP ON A REPUBLICAN STRONGHOLD

Talarico, who is challenging Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton in a closely watched U.S. Senate contest, had not been seen publicly in person at a campaign event since late September. His last in-person event was a Sept. 26 news conference in Carrollton addressing rising gas prices.

Talarico's campaign attributed the absence to a severe case of the flu. However, the prolonged pause drew sharp criticism from Republicans, including President Donald Trump.

HECKLERS INTERRUPT TRUMP TEXAS RALLY MULTIPLE TIMES

In a post on Truth Social, Trump said the Democrat was "MISSING IN ACTION."

"TalaFREAKo has been missing for 12 days! Now, after looking for him throughout all of Texas, and beyond, probably even weirder places than anyone would think possible, he put out a statement that he has the 'flu,'" Trump wrote.

"12 days is a long time to rid yourself of the so-called flu bug. What’s going on?" he added. "We need a Senator that’s a proven Champion like one that has been, without question, the Greatest Attorney General in the History of Texas, and one of the Greatest in the U.S.A."

Talarico’s campaign pushed back on the characterization that he had been absent from the campaign trail for nearly two weeks, saying he attended a Zoom on Sept. 30 with the U.S. Hispanic Business Council after canceling an in-person event. The campaign argued that because he attended that Zoom, his absence was closer to nine days.

COWBOYS LEGEND RANDY WHITE ENDORSES KEN PAXTON, WARNS JAMES TALARICO ‘CAN’T BE TRUSTED’

Talarico's last public event was a Sept. 26 campaign event in Texas, where he held a news conference in Carrollton. On Sept. 28, he attended a fundraiser in New York City.

The next day, he said he'd been diagnosed with the flu.

Talarico's absence also prompted Paxton to target his opponent’s absence while on the campaign trail.

"Where is James Talarico?" Paxton asked during a campaign rally in San Antonio.

PAXTON VENTS OVER LACK OF CAMPAIGN CONTROL AS DC ESTABLISHMENT HE ONCE BATTLED COMES TO HIS AID

Talarico's campaign confirmed he expects to return to a full in-person schedule through the weekend ahead of an Oct. 14 CNN town hall.

The campaign previously noted that, prior to his illness, Talarico had already completed more than 100 public campaign events across the state.

item.title: Super Bowl LXI gets Pat McAfee treatment as ESPN adds alternate broadcast

item.title: Former Obama advisor tells divided Maine Democrats to 'get over your s---' and win the race
item.description: Former Obama strategists urge Maine Democrats to unite behind Troy Jackson, warning internal party feuds could cost them a critical Senate seat.
item.content:encoded:
Former aides to President Barack Obama discussed divisions among Maine Democrats over the party's troubled U.S. Senate race against incumbent Republican Sen. Susan Collins, with a warning to Democrats to "get over your s---."

Maine's Senate race has drawn national attention after Democrats replaced their initial candidate, Graham Platner, due to sexual assault allegations against him. His replacement, Troy Jackson, has faced controversies of his own.

Even so, Obama, the former boss of the "Pod Save America" hosts, recently released an endorsement video urging Maine voters not to sit out the election. The hosts discussed why Obama might have chosen that message.

Former Obama strategist Dan Pfeiffer told his co-hosts that "it is true, and we have — this has been sort of mysterious to both of us — that there are a significant number of people in Maine who seem not to like Troy Jackson, including some Democrats."

DEM WHO ABANDONED PLATNER AFTER SEX ASSAULT CLAIM NOW SCRAMBLES FOR HIS VOTERS

"Yeah," former Obama speechwriter Jon Favreau agreed. "That’s my biggest worry."

Pfeiffer offered his assessment of the feuds between Democrats, saying, "And, so I think a little whether there are people who supported Platner who didn't like Platner being gone or the process by which we got here, or people who were supporting Mills who don't like any of this and Mills and Jackson do not like each other. And as of, like, two weeks ago, Mills had not endorsed Jackson and Jackson had not asked for the endorsement.

"Everyone get over your s---, and let's try to win this race. 

"I think there is some sense or fear, maybe, that some of the people who are not enthusiastic about Jackson for some reason because of how this process played out may sit out and so just like ‘get in here, get in the fight,’" Pfeiffer added of Obama’s video. 

"I don't know if that's a real concern or not, but if I was trying to find a reason why that line would be in there, that would be it."

"Yeah, I would say to all the Maine Democrats out there, I know it's been a rough one, but look to Michigan," Favreau said. "They had an extremely divisive primary, and you had Gretchen Whitmer … out there with Abdul [El-Sayed] this week.

"Haley Stevens has been saying great things," he continued, noting Democrats in Michigan have been coming together after initially being divided.

"And I really wish — I do think that Troy Jackson would probably benefit from more Maine Democrats and national Democrats kind of, you know, because, like, Maine is the kind of state that, again, it wants to go Democratic," Favreau added. 

"They want — those voters want a Democratic Senate. That's what they're telling.

"Even The New York Times poll that showed Collins ahead, you had people — most people — wanting a Democratic Senate," he said. 

"So, like, I feel like the Democrats there just have to be reminded that, like, this is our guy, and this is our ticket to a Democratic Senate and not a Republican Senate."

MAINE DEMOCRATS CROWN TROY JACKSON AS PLATNER REPLACEMENT AS FRESH SCRUTINY CLOUDS SENATE RESET

Democratic strategist Julian Epstein told Fox News Digital, "Socialist revolutionaries all seem to be a little bit weird for one reason or another. Going MIA here, a Nazi tattoo there, refusing to denounce terrorists. Marry this with the mainstreaming in the Democratic Party of this lust for the centralized, command and control economic decision-making and the further expansion of a welfare state that is completely broke and headed towards a kind of complete breakdown that mimics Europe's current dysfunction.

"The political and consultant class doesn't seem to care about these things," he continued. "They always find a way to rationalize. To them, it's less about principle and more about power. If these revolutionary candidates don't win, it means less power and money for the left and its apparatchiks. It seems like it's just about power at any cost these days. The Beltway money barge has a strange way of warping the sensibilities."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Jesse Arm, vice president of external affairs at the Manhattan Institute, said the Obama administration alumni were coping.

"The ‘Pod Save America’ bros are just struggling to cope," he told Fox News Digital. "Susan Collins is overperforming because Maine voters know she’s a sensible moderate who calls balls and strikes.

"Collins has been an independent maverick throughout her career, and Maine voters appreciate that about her."

item.title: Trump gives raw reaction after finding out about Mike Ditka's death: 'A tough cookie'
item.description: Trump called Mike Ditka "a tough cookie" and "a winner" after learning of the Hall of Fame Chicago Bears coach's death on the South Lawn Friday.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump was caught by surprise on the South Lawn before heading to Syracuse on Friday.

Before making the trip north with Mike Tyson and New York Yankees president Randy Levine, the press pool informed Trump that famed Chicago Bears head coach Mike Ditka had died.

The news issued a raw reaction from the president.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"Oh, he did? He was a great guy. He was with me all the way. He was tough," Trump said. "Mike Ditka — that's a sad one."

"He was great. He was a big supporter of mine, and he was a winner. He was a tough cookie."

Ditka supported Trump ahead of the 2016 election.

Ditka coached the famous 1985 Bears that rampaged through the NFL with an 18-1 record, losing only to the Miami Dolphins, and then going on to a Super Bowl title.

The death of one of the NFL's greats was announced Friday morning by his family in a statement.

"It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend, Mike Ditka," the statement said. "While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears’ Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family.

LEGENDARY BEARS HEAD COACH MIKE DITKA DEAD AT 86

Ditka was a great tight end who won the Super Bowl with Dallas, and was a Super Bowl winning coach with the Chicago Bears. He also became something of an iconic figure as fans and celebrities copied his look and imitated his no-nonsense talk.

Drafted by the Chicago Bears in 1961, he became the first modern receiving tight end and the first tight end selected to the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

Ditka won NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year in 1961 and made five consecutive Pro Bowls from 1961-65 and earned five All-Pro selections.

He played for the Bears from 1961-66, the Philadelphia Eagles from 1967-68 and the Dallas Cowboys from 1969-72, finishing with 427 receptions, 5,812 yards and 43 touchdowns.

Ditka played on teams that won the 1963 NFL championship with Chicago and Super Bowl VI with Dallas following the 1971 season.

He retired as a player after the 1972 season, entered the College Football Hall of Fame in 1986 and the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1988.

He became Chicago’s head coach in 1982 and was named NFL Coach of the Year in 1985 and 1988, coached the Bears through 1992 and later led the New Orleans Saints from 1997-99.

OutKick's Armando Salguero and Ryan Canfield contributed to this report.

item.title: Hollywood feeling more hopeful amid a push for film tax credits and Paramount staying put, filmmaker says
item.description: California expands its film and television tax credits and launches a post-production incentive as Hollywood fights to keep jobs in Los Angeles.
item.content:encoded:
Now that Paramount is staying put in Los Angeles and state and federal lawmakers are pushing for expanded film tax credits, Hollywood insiders are seeing a glimmer of hope.

On Wednesday, California Gov. Gavin Newsom highlighted the state’s latest efforts to bolster its entertainment industry, including a new post-production tax credit, an expanded film and television tax credit and new protections for performers against the use of AI-generated content.

"California is the home of entertainment, full stop," Newsom said in a statement. "We’re not just protecting that legacy; we’re investing in its future by expanding our film and television tax credit, launching a new post-production credit and standing up for performers in the age of AI.

"We’re making sure independent filmmakers and the next generation of storytellers and creators have a real shot to build, hire and produce right here in California," he added. "More productions, more good jobs, more California stories told by California workers."

CALIFORNIA LAW PUTS DIGITAL FINGERPRINTS ON AI FAKES

At the federal level, a bipartisan coalition of lawmakers is working on a tax credit for film and television productions. The bill is expected to be introduced in Congress in early November, with its backers aiming to secure passage by Dec. 11, before the current Congress concludes its work. If passed, the credit would take effect in 2027 and could be used alongside state production incentives.

Championed by President Donald Trump, the legislation has also received support from one of his most formidable political opponents, Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif. Schiff led the first impeachment effort against Trump and has remained a vocal critic of his leadership.

"I am in strong agreement with the President," Schiff said on X. "Congress should immediately take up and pass a federal film tax incentive to bring back these good-paying jobs that we've lost to other countries."

NETFLIX CHIEF ADMITS TRUMP IS HELPING SHOWBIZ INDUSTRY AS FEDERAL TAX CREDIT BILL AIMS TO FUEL HOLLYWOOD JOBS

Filmmaker Paul Kampf, a 30-year veteran of the entertainment industry, described California’s incentives as "a really good start."

"No matter where you make your film, whether it's Georgia, Delaware, Puerto Rico or Europe, if you can do your post-production in California, you're keeping jobs here, especially in independent films," Kampf told Fox News Digital. 

"We should be incentivizing filmmakers in America to stay in America. And we should also incentivize filmmakers who are outside of America to do their post here."

Kampf, who has produced four feature films and a documentary in Serbia before embarking on his sixth project there, titled "Harvest," has also found himself embroiled in a situation in which a company owned by the Serbian government released the film in Eastern Europe without his permission.

"This film is an example of what happens if we don't protect Americans and entice Americans to film here," Kampf said.

In California, 35 films, including 28 independent projects, have received production incentives for filming in the state. The sequel to Lionsgate’s blockbuster 2026 hit "Michael" is among the projects, along with a new Pixar film.

FILM PRODUCER SAYS 'MADE IN AMERICA' MOVIES CAN HELP REVIVE HOLLYWOOD'S STRUGGLING INDUSTRY

All told, the projects are expected to generate more than $1 billion in direct production spending, according to the California Film Commission.

"Through our tax credit program, we’re helping bring these stories to the screen while keeping the jobs, investment and production that bring them to life right here in California," Colleen Bell, director of the California Film Commission, said Wednesday in a statement.

Kampf, who has made films in several countries, told Fox News Digital California had long been arrogant about its position in the industry, assuming it held a monopoly on filmmaking.

"I've made movies all over the world. I don't make movies in LA. I live here. I lived the taxes of LA and California, and I live the sort of challenges of lifestyle here," he said. 

"I think Hollywood needs a facelift, and it's no pun intended. It needs to be seen as a place that is invigorating and investing in filmmaking again.

"Realistically, what I can say is the tax incentives in America are really maybe the best bipartisan entertainment bill that I've seen in the last 10 years."

item.title: Texas legend has sky-high hopes for Longhorns ahead of Red River Rivalry game vs Oklahoma
item.description: Colt McCoy calls the Texas Longhorns' current roster arguably the most talented ever as they enter the Red River Rivalry ranked No. 1 at 4-0.
item.content:encoded:
The Red River Rivalry makes its return on Saturday, and someone all too familiar with the big game was back in Dallas on Friday gearing up for his former Texas Longhorns to continue their national title hopes.

Colt McCoy never quite reached the promised land in Austin, but he did have the upper hand in the matchup, going 3-1 in his four years, including the 45-35 victory when his Texas squad was fifth in the country, and the Oklahoma Sooners were ranked No. 1.

Texas has won three of the last four matchups after losing 10 of the previous 13, including the 2018 Big 12 Championship Game.

"Just the history of this game, right in the middle between both schools, played in Dallas, played in the Cotton Bowl, that place, I mean, you just feel the sanctity of that place when you walk down the tunnel, the shared tunnel. The fans are split down the middle, it's always played in October, it's kind of the kickoff into your conference," McCoy said to Fox News Digital in an interview Friday. "It's just a really, really special game, at least the ones that I was a part of.

"And the beauty of rivalries is that you may be the best team in the country, but if you don't strap it up and play that day or if you're off that day, like you got problems. So, I love it. Just being back here is pretty surreal. It's a really, really fun weekend."

McCoy was hanging out with some fans on behalf of Fanatics, which offers official Red River Rivalry merchandise.

"I had a great time, man. Texas fans are the best, dude. They show up everywhere. It's a whole lot of fun to engage with them. And then especially this weekend, this was the one game on your calendar every year that you circled, and you thought about, and you got nervous about all the things. This is a fun one," McCoy said.

"Fanatics is great. Listen, it's a wonderful brand. The gear is incredible. The fans showed out. There was like a million fans in the Texas line and nobody on the Oklahoma side. So, this is exactly what I wanted."

McCoy admitted that it was tough to stay focused on the game before the Red River Rivalry knowing what was soon on the table.

"Generally, we didn't play great if I can remember right," McCoy said (he went 3-1 in games preceding the rivalry, the loss being a 41-21 upset by unranked Kansas State when they were No. 7). "But then the moment you get back in the locker room after that game, they've got Boomer Sooner playing and they play it all week, and by the time you get to the game, you're just ready to punch somebody in the mouth."

But when McCoy was a third-round pick in the NFL Draft, he had no choice but to throw the rivalry aside.

"I got to admit, I've had some amazing teammates that came out of Oklahoma over the years. Trent Williams for a long time, he is a phenomenal teammate. He may be the greatest left tackle ever. Still playing 17 years at an All-Pro level. It really is unbelievable. A great guy, great friend. Played with Adrian Peterson for a couple years, Tress Way, amazing punter. Kyler Murray is my boy. So, there's unfortunately been some really good dudes come out of Oklahoma."

But now that he's out of the game, it's all Texas and no Oklahoma once again, and he feels like this year's squad has what it takes to bring home its first national title in over two decades.

"Listen, we're 4-0 and number one in the country, and they hadn't really clicked yet, right? The sky's the limit for this team. They're super talented. They're well coached. They kind of have all the makings from both sides of the ball to be really special. And I certainly think that they have a lot of confidence internally, and they just got to go do it. And I really think they will," said McCoy.

"We had a 10-year dry spell that was hard. I think right now what I'll give you is I do think that this is arguably the most talented roster that Texas has had. Just when you look across the board, you look at the coaching staff, you look at the players, you look at just the straight talent, like man-to-man, they're never going to go into a game and be outmatched. item.title: At least one person isn't concerned about Cam Skattebo getting injured, and his name is Cam Skattebo

item.content:encoded:

item.title: Daniel Lurie argues progressivism led San Francisco astray on public safety, drug crisis
item.description: Daniel Lurie says San Francisco got "entrapped in our progressive values" and got to a point where the city wasn't taking stock of its problems.
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie said Thursday that the city had lost its way and was focused on the wrong things, arguing that the California city was "entrapped in our progressive values."

"We lost our way as a city," he told CNN's Dana Bash in an interview. "We were focused on the wrong things, and today we're focused on common sense. We're focused on good governance. We're focused on delivering results for the people of San Francisco. I said from day one, public safety was going to be my number one priority. The crisis on our streets, the mental health and drug crisis is another top priority of mine. And I want to get the basics of governance right." 

Lurie, a moderate Democrat and heir to the Levi Strauss fortune, was elected in 2024 after defeating incumbent London Breed.

"I mean, we got so entrapped in our progressive values and talking about progressivism, that we weren't taking stock of what was happening on our streets," he told Bash. "We had 810 people die of overdose in San Francisco three years ago. There's nothing progressive about that. There's nothing progressive about 30,000 car break-ins. Everyone had to deal with whether or not their car was going to be broken into," the mayor said, adding that the number of car break-ins had dropped 90%.

SAN FRANCISCO STILL HASN'T RECOVERED SINCE PANDEMIC EXODUS: REPORT

Bash asked Lurie about progressivism again, specifically how he defined the word. The mayor said he supported progressive values, such as taking care of the city's immigrants, and the LGBTQ+ community.

"But, we got to a point where we said, 'Well, it's that person's right to be on the street using drugs,' or is that person — it's okay for someone to just go in and take what they want from a small business," he said.

"In my mind, that's not progressive," Lurie continued. "There's nothing progressive about small businesses having to shutter up because they're a victim of crime over and over again. There's nothing progressive, as I said before, about 810 people dying of overdose. I'm not going to walk by somebody on the street and not do anything anymore."

NEWSOM BLASTS DEMOCRATS FOR THEIR 'VICTIM MINDSET' THAT ENABLED HOMELESS CRISIS

President Donald Trump praised Lurie during a cabinet meeting in March for "really trying" to improve San Francisco since taking office.

"I know they have a mayor who’s trying very hard. He’s a Democrat, but he’s trying very hard," Trump said at the time.

Socialism has been on the rise in the U.S., as several states have seen socialist candidates win their primary elections. In some places, progressive candidates were rejected for more moderate voices as well.

Democratic strategist Kaivan Shroff told Fox News Digital that even more liberal voices were calling out progressivism.

"Lurie is right, and it’s not just more moderate voices like his calling this stuff out — we’ve seen AOC try to distance herself from ‘Woke 1’ as well," he said. "Some on the left have absolutely allowed themselves to get bullied into silence and, as funny and extreme a case as it was — that is how you get stories like that Massachusetts lesbian bar with the masking debacle."

"Progressive policies are increasingly popular across the country, particularly on economic issues in these hard economic times," Shroff continued. "But there is also a sense that the DSA left can’t get out of its own way and can never be satisfied."

"It’s not popular to say, but there is a real contingent on the left that uses these movements to center themselves and try to control others — beyond actual progressive aims," he added. "That is what Lurie is hitting on here and that is in some sense what happened in SF before his tenure. Yes, we want policies that are pro-family, pro-worker, pro-immigrant — that doesn’t mean letting the loudest voices dictate everything at the cost of a functioning city."

item.title: Tyreek Hill changes divorce battery trial testimony, claiming he didn't push wife but was verbally abusive
item.description: Tyreek Hill admitted to verbally abusing wife Lakeeta Vaccaro during intense cross-examination in their Miami-Dade County divorce battery trial.
item.content:encoded:
NFL free agent wide receiver Tyreek Hill spent his second day on the stand of his divorce battery trial admitting to verbally abusing his wife Lakeeta Vaccaro but insisting he had not harmed her physically.

And through the former player's testimony on Friday, the attorneys for Vaccaro have not yet produced incontrovertible evidence of physical violence by Hill against their client.

Instead, what we saw on Friday was Hill on the stand trying to erase a significant problem he created for himself the day before, while Vaccaro's attorneys pressed the issue.

TYREEK HILL DENIES MOST ABUSE CLAIMS BUT ADMITS TO SHOVING WIFE INTO WALL

Hill on Friday morning changed his testimony from Thursday in which he admitted to pushing Vaccaro, which caused a hole in the wall of their Sunny Isle condominium.

"I told her don't you ever touch me again in your life. I pushed her against the wall. And I tried to force her to get off me," Hill testified on Thursday. "I created a hole in the wall, trying to force her to get off me that night."

His testimony on Friday changed to a door caused the hole.

"The door, the main door," Hill told his attorney. "I was trying to evade [Vaccaro], but I'm not trying to harm her or push her against the wall or, like, do anything crazy. As I was trying to evade, I put a hole in the wall with the door."

Hill's attorneys also made sure Hill explicitly denied ever hurting his wife's breasts, which Vaccaro alleged on the stand earlier in the trial.

But Vaccaro's attorneys, on cross-examination, then tried to muddy up Hill further.

The plaintiff attorneys got Hill to admit he spoke in an explicitly insulting manner about his wife to her and some of his friends.

"The language, I'm gonna take that all on this end, I'm not proud of that," Hill testified. "I am ashamed. I don't even go back home because my marriage failed ... The language was terrible. Was terrible. I wish I could have been better in every single moment, but I'm not perfect.

"The only thing I can do is learn from it and move forward and never talk to my co-parent like that again."

Vaccaro's attorneys pointed to multiple instances in which Hill's testimony Thursday contradicted statements he made during his deposition.

They impeached Hill on his testimony that Vaccaro may have had something to do with a house fire at the couple's Southwest Ranches home in Broward County when, in fact, the cause was determined to be a child playing with a lighter.

They attempted to impeach Hill's contention on the stand Thursday that Vaccaro was "stealing" money from the family account.

They impeached Hill on his suggestion on the stand Thursday that Vaccaro had something to do with him performing worse after the marriage than before, making the point it was Tua Tagovailoa throwing the passes and coach Mike McDaniel calling the plays.

"She wasn't calling the plays on the field, but at home she was calling the plays" Hill said, sticking by his guns. "If you got a real good support system at home, that's what's important."

Hill did, however, admit that saying Vaccaro played a role in his diminished performance was his opinion.

"I'm not sitting here blaming wifey for that, bro," Hill said. "I'm not."

Attorneys then impeached Hill's testimony blaming Vaccaro for Hill's mom becoming homeless. In fact, Hill moved his grandmother, which he refers to as his mom, into a hotel.

Vaccaro's attorneys used video from a nanny camera inside the house to try to prove Hill emotionally hurt his wife — and Hill acknowledged that he did.

"In that moment, yes," Hill agreed. "In that moment."

Did Hill want to break Vaccaro mentally, Vaccaro's attorney asked?

"That's not what I wanted to do, bro," Hill replied.

But Hill admitted he verbally abused his wife.

"When you say verbally, you mean with words, right? Hill asked. "Oh, yes sir."

The trial in Miami-Dade County court is ongoing and reconvenes on Monday.

item.title: Cars flipped, school devastated as violent twister rips through popular city
item.description: Dramatic footage captures the Marsala tornado overturning vehicles and destroying a school as officials call it the worst storm in living memory.
item.content:encoded:
A powerful tornado tore through a popular vacation destination Friday, overturning vehicles and damaging buildings — and leaving at least two people seriously injured.

The tornado swept through Marsala, a city on the western coast of Sicily, roughly 55 miles southwest of Palermo.

Dramatic footage showed the tornado swirling through the city, sending debris flying as powerful winds battered the area.

TERRIFYING SCENE UNFOLDS AT SIX FLAGS AS STORM-TOPPLED TREE SENDS 4 GUESTS TO HOSPITAL

The tornado overturned vehicles and seriously injured at least two people on Friday, Reuters reported. 

A school was also said to be damaged by the storm, along with at least one house. Damage was reported in nearby Petrosino and Mazara del Vallo, as well as Marsala.

Video reviewed by Reuters also showed blown-out windows and a partially collapsed ceiling at a school in Marsala, while cars and trucks lay overturned.

In addition, downed utility poles littered the streets.

ISLAND GETAWAY HIT WITH URGENT WARNING AS HURRICANE DAMAGE LEAVES TRAVELERS WITHOUT POWER

Salvatore Cocina, the head of Sicily's Civil Protection agency, told Reuters the scene was "almost like an American tornado."

"Nothing this violent has been seen in living memory," he said. 

"It once again highlights the issue of extreme weather events, a characteristic of recent years due to the climate crisis," he added.

Sicily's Civil Protection agency warned in September that a recent heat wave could contribute to extreme weather, Reuters reported.

In a translated Friday statement obtained by Fox News Digital, Sicily's regional councilor for education, Mimmo Turano, said officials were working to secure funding for repairs after the tornado severely damaged the school in Marsala.

"The situation is serious, the school is no longer there and many companies have been affected by this tragedy," Turano said.

"Together with President Schifani, we will implement every intervention useful to support the entire area," he added.

The tornado is the latest in a string of dangerous incidents to strike the Italian island in recent months.

Earlier this summer, an American tourist was stranded in Sicily after volcanic activity from Mount Etna disrupted flights, forcing her to scramble for an alternative route home to New York.

In August, a 29-year-old American tourist from Kansas was killed by a lightning strike while hiking Sicily's Mount Etna.

item.title: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles suffers health scare after taking helmet to the stomach during celebration
item.description: Tampa Bay Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles took a helmet to the stomach during celebrations and went down to a knee while grimacing in pain.
item.content:encoded:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles had every reason to celebrate after his team pulled off an impressive upset win over the Dallas Cowboys.

So, when he was seen grimacing in pain on the sideline while down on one knee as the clock wound down on the Bucs’ 24-16 win Thursday at AT&T Stadium, it was an alarming scene.

However, it turns out the 62-year-old was in pain because he took a helmet to the stomach during the Buccaneers’ celebration after they intercepted Dak Prescott to help seal the win, according to ESPN. Bowles said he will be OK moving forward, according to the report.

For Bowles, taking a helmet to the stomach may be a small price to pay for the Bucs’ first win of the season. They entered the game as heavy underdogs, going on the road on a short week while starting Jalon Daniels at quarterback, an undrafted rookie making his second career start in relief of Baker Mayfield.

The Bucs dominated time of possession, holding the ball for more than 39 minutes. They also forced three turnovers (two Prescott interceptions and a fumble by KeVontae Turpin on a kickoff return) and outgained the Cowboys by more than 50 yards.

Daniels completed 19 of his 25 passes for 189 yards and a touchdown. Running back Bucky Irving was outstanding in the win, running for 165 yards on 21 carries with a rushing touchdown, and catching two passes for 10 yards and a receiving touchdown.

For the Buccaneers, Thursday night’s win over the Cowboys was much needed after a dismal start to the season. They had lost their first four games by a combined 20 points, hanging around in every game but not doing enough to come out on top.

Bowles will look to have his squad build on some positive momentum — and avoid taking another helmet to the stomach — when they play the Pittsburgh Steelers next Sunday.

item.title: Texas think tank accuses Houston parent coalition of using 'socialist' tactics to push radical agenda
item.description: The Texas Public Policy Foundation accuses a Houston education coalition of using socialist-aligned tactics to push radical policies in HISD schools.
item.content:encoded:
A conservative Texas think tank is warning against a Houston education advocacy coalition, accusing the group of using socialist-aligned tactics to push radical policies in public schools.

In a report released by the Texas Public Policy Foundation (TPPF), researchers argue that Community Voices for Public Education (CVPE) — which presents itself as a grassroots group of parents, teachers and community members — acts as a front for teachers' unions and far-left organizations working to preserve the status quo.

"There are several policies that they're advocating for which are questionable at best, but very harmful," Kate Bierly, campaign director for TPPF's Next Generation Texas Campaign, told Fox News Digital.

WATCHDOG REPORT EXPOSES TEACHERS UNION 'POLITICAL MACHINE' FUNNELING MORE THAN $1 BILLION TO LIBERAL CAUSES

CVPE has been an outspoken opponent of the state's 2023 takeover of the Houston Independent School District (HISD), Texas's largest school district. The Texas Education Agency (TEA) intervened following years of academic underperformance at select campuses — a move that drew sharp accusations of political overreach from critics.

State metrics, however, show noticeable academic gains since the intervention. Reading and math scores on the State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness (STAAR) improved among grades 3 through 8 over the past three school years, while the number of A- and B-rated campuses in HISD jumped from 93 to 197.

SHOCKING PERCENTAGE OF DEMOCRATS IDENTIFY AS 'DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS' ACCORDING TO NEW POLL: 'TOXIC POLICIES'

"F-rated campuses went from 56 to five, and the whole district moved from a C rating to a B rating," Bierly said. "The results were amazing. But from this, several critics emerged ... suggesting destructive replacement policies. One of the main groups behind these proposals is CVPE."

The local group, Bierly said, uses tactics similar to those employed by the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), which has gained traction in recent years as a political force with the election of several DSA-endorsed candidates across various levels of government.

DSA CO-CHAIR PUSHES BACK ON SOVIET UNION COMPARISONS, WANTS PRISONS TO BE 'LESS NECESSARY'

Beyond opposing the state takeover, CVPE advocates against mandatory STAAR testing and urges parents to boycott the exams. The group also calls for divesting from campus policing — ending student arrests except in severe cases such as murder — and encourages participation in walkouts and political protests.

TPPF contends that CVPE actively instructs parents on how to organize student demonstrations outside schools, while CVPE maintains that peaceful advocacy is essential to improving school environments and curricula.

"Some of the things they are advocating for is that parents should boycott the STAAR exam because the test allegedly supports racism and inequality," Bierly added. "Scrapping this testing removes a key pathway for low-income kids to access advanced academic tracks."

FAR-LEFT ACTIVIST CONFERENCE AT TEACHERS UNION HQ RAISES CLASSROOM CONCERNS

CVPE defends its platform, maintaining that restorative justice and expanded mental health resources foster safer learning environments than punitive measures, insisting "HISD students should be heard and not herded."

Ruth Kravetz, co-founder of CVPE, pushed back on both TPPF’s report and the state's academic claims. Speaking to Fox News Digital, Kravetz dismissed assertions that her group relies on DSA tactics, emphasizing that CVPE supporters span the political spectrum.

"Some of those parents are Republicans. Some are Democrats, some are socialists, and some are unaffiliated," Kravetz said.

POWERFUL TEACHERS' UNIONS SHARE STRIKING LINK WITH STATES STRUGGLING TO TEACH KIDS TO READ

Kravetz also criticized high-stakes standardized testing, arguing that it fails to improve student outcomes.

"It undermines educational quality," Kravetz said. "It narrows instruction and reduces deeper, more meaningful learning ... I don't think any parent ever said, ‘I hope my kid grows up to be able to fill in a multiple-choice test well.’"

Kravetz previously challenged the "Texas Miracle" touted by HISD Superintendent Mike Miles and Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, alleging that recent test improvements were artificially-engineered.

"The truth is that HISD’s Mike Miles didn’t allow qualified students to even take Algebra I," Kravetz said. "This skewed the STAAR results and played a shell game with scores. Most importantly, they denied opportunities to countless kids just to make the numbers look better."

HISD did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: Attorney for alleged victim of trans athlete sexual assault says SCOTUS fight can help set Title IX precedent
item.description: Kallie Keeler's Supreme Court wrestling case could force 23 states to restrict transgender athletes in girls' sports under Title IX, her lawyer says.
item.content:encoded:
A Washington high school wrestler’s Supreme Court fight could help bring restrictions on transgender athletes in girls’ sports to 23 states, an attorney representing her told OutKick.

Alliance Defending Freedom (ADF) senior counsel Hal Frampton said the ultimate objective is a ruling establishing that Title IX requires a protected female sports category, with consequences beyond the immediate request to protect wrestler Kallie Keeler.

"And the hope would be then that that would force all 23 of those states to enact policies protecting women and girls, protecting the female category, and simply getting back to the common sense notion that women's sports are for women," Frampton said.

WASHINGTON FAMILY REQUESTS SCOTUS INJUNCTION AFTER DAUGHTER WAS ALLEGEDLY SEXUALLY ASSAULTED BY TRANS ATHLETE

Keeler, identified in court as K.M.K., and her mother, Stephanie Lynne Brown, are seeking intervention after Keeler alleged she was sexually assaulted by a transgender opponent during a girls’ wrestling match in December 2025.

"Ultimately, the goal is a ruling from the Supreme Court that says that Title IX requires fairness and safety for women and girls," Frampton said.

Asked whether that broader objective could be accomplished through the current Supreme Court application or would require further steps, Frampton called it "a huge step toward accomplishing that goal."

The application seeks an injunction pending appeal and alternatively asks the justices to take up the case before the Ninth Circuit finishes reviewing it. A temporary order protecting Keeler would not, by itself, impose new eligibility policies on 23 states.

INSIDE THE SUPREME COURT BATTLE TO 'SAVE WOMEN'S SPORTS'

The distinction matters because the Ninth Circuit said the Supreme Court’s recent West Virginia v. B.P.J. decision left open whether schools may allow biological males who identify as female to participate in girls’ and women’s sports. Frampton’s goal would address that unresolved question.

For Keeler, Frampton said, the immediate concern is returning to wrestling before her remaining high school seasons slip away.

"We filed the emergency application with the Supreme Court because it's really the only way to get Callie and her family relief in advance of wrestling season," he said.

Frampton emphasized that the emergency request seeks protection for Keeler rather than monetary damages, though he left open the possibility of pursuing damages later.

"For right now, all we're saying is while this case is pending," give her assurance she can compete without being matched against a male athlete, he said. He accused Washington officials of refusing to compromise: "From the very beginning, there's been no effort to compromise, to accommodate Callie, to appreciate what she's been through."

Justice Elena Kagan has requested a response to the application by 4 p.m. EDT Oct. 13. The request remained pending as of Friday. Washington’s wrestling season begins in mid-November.

The Ninth Circuit denied emergency relief Sept. 25, finding the family had not established an immediate emergency or a sufficiently strong likelihood of success. It also raised concerns about other students’ privacy and the breadth of the requested relief, while noting the district had said Keeler could forfeit matches without district-imposed adverse consequences.

Frampton rejected the privacy justification and accused Washington officials of refusing to accommodate Keeler.

"From the very beginning, there's been no effort to compromise, to accommodate Callie, to appreciate what she's been through," he said.

The WIAA previously said it would follow state law allowing participation by gender identity and revise its policies if that law changes.

Pierce County prosecutors declined to charge Keeler’s opponent, concluding they could not prove third-degree rape beyond a reasonable doubt or overcome a consent defense arising from case law on athletic contests. The prosecutor emphasized that the decision did not mean approval of the alleged conduct.

Frampton said the experience has taken a toll on Keeler and her family, including her transfer to another school.

"She ultimately had to change schools in order to get away from the harassment and bullying and the just lack of concern from the administration, which is not easy for any high school student to do," he said.

Still, he described the family as determined to continue pursuing the case.

"High school careers are fleeting. She's already a junior. Blink and it'll be over. And we just don't want her to miss out on the opportunity to compete in high school athletics," Frampton said.

The family’s request has drawn support from 24 states, led by Iowa and Idaho, which filed a brief Oct. 7 arguing that allowing biological males into female sports denies girls Title IX protections.

The Independent Council on Women’s Sports (ICONS) and its members also filed an amicus brief Oct. 8 supporting Keeler’s emergency request, arguing that school administrators bear responsibility under Title IX for protecting female athletes. The brief contends that lost athletic opportunities cause irreparable harm and that privacy concerns should not prevent schools from identifying competitors’ biological sex.

"It is unreasonable for school administrators to attempt to shift the burden of protecting girls in school sports to parents and children," the brief states.

OutKick reached out to the Washington Interscholastic Activities Association, Puyallup School District and the Washington Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction for comment on Frampton’s latest statements.

In its previous response to the injunction request, the WIAA said it would continue following Washington law allowing students to compete according to their gender identity and could revise its policies if the law changes. "The WIAA will not comment further on a matter in litigation," the association said.

The superintendent’s office said it does not oversee athletics but is responsible for communicating and enforcing applicable law. "OSPI will continue to uphold Washington’s current law unless or until the law changes." It added that it had issued no non-privileged statement, board notice or guidance to schools or staff regarding the appeal.

Puyallup School District previously acknowledged receiving the Supreme Court application and said it would respond if requested by the Court, "in accordance with the Court’s rules and established process." Its statement did not specify whether it would oppose the application or provide the advance notice sought by Keeler’s mother.

item.title: Michael Douglas says Kirk Douglas gave him $10,000 at 21 and told him he was on his own
item.description: Michael Douglas reveals on "Jimmy Kimmel Live" how Kirk Douglas handed him $10,000 at age 21 and told him he was on his own in his new memoir.
item.content:encoded:

"I was 21 years old. He said, ‘Son,’ and he wrote me a check, $10,000. item.title: 'SNL' writer's missing sister case leads homicide detectives to Joshua Tree months after family's murder claim
item.description: LAPD homicide detectives searched Joshua Tree for evidence in the disappearance of Christina Downer, sister of "Saturday Night Live" writer Jimmy Fowlie.
item.content:encoded:

"The LAPD has informed our family that Christina is no longer alive, and the case has officially transitioned from a missing person to a homicide investigation," Fowlie wrote. "Our prayers for her to be found safely have transformed into prayers for the truth to be revealed and for those responsible to be held accountable."

FAMILY OF CRITICALLY MISSING DC MOTHER SAYS POLICE STILL TREATING HOME AS ACTIVE CRIME SCENE

item.title: Costco slashes price of popular holiday treat after shoppers balked at last year's hike
item.description: Costco's Kirkland Signature Peppermint Bark is back for $12.99 after last year's controversial $16.99 price hike sparked shopper backlash online.
item.content:encoded:
While most grocery prices continue to climb, one seasonal Costco favorite is back at a lower price than last year.

The Kirkland Signature Peppermint Bark has returned to shelves even earlier in the season than usual, according to shoppers on social media and recent reports.

The holiday treat, which features layers of dark and white chocolate topped with crushed peppermint candy, is sold in a 21-ounce container for $12.99 at some locations, or less than $1.75 per serving, though availability and pricing can vary. The same container sold for $16.99 in 2025, according to reports, up from $9.99 in 2023.

COSTCO BRINGS BACK A FAN-FAVORITE FOOD COURT TREAT AFTER YEARS OFF THE MENU

Either way, the sweet and minty dessert costs far less than some specialty alternatives, like Williams-Sonoma's version, which costs about $35.

There was an outcry from shoppers last holiday season when the 21-ounce package jumped from $9.99 to $16.99. One Reddit user wrote that it was "good, but not for $16.99," while others said they skipped it after the increase or preferred the pricier Williams-Sonoma bark.

This year's reported $12.99 price brings the treat closer to its former value, even if it remains above its 2023 price.

COSTCO SPARKS BAGEL BACKLASH AMONG CUSTOMERS AS DOWNSIZED PACKS IGNITE PRICING DEBATE

Fans have long praised the candy cane-topped treat as a holiday staple that complements dessert platters, makes for an easy hostess gift or elevates a mug of hot cocoa.

"The Kirkland brand peppermint bark in the bakery is absolutely fire," one Reddit user wrote, adding that it was "way better than" Ghirardelli's individually wrapped version.

Costco has also begun restocking Kirkland Signature organic Madagascar vanilla beans, which give home bakers 20 whole pods for $9.69. The seasonal baking find works out to roughly 48 cents per bean and can be used in holiday desserts or to make homemade vanilla extract, according to reports.

item.title: Bill Maher warns Democrats still haven't 'renounced their crazy,' says it could spell trouble in 2028
item.description: Comedian Bill Maher warned the Democratic Party hasn't "renounced their crazy" and says the far left could misinterpret midterm wins as backing communism.
item.content:encoded:
Comedian Bill Maher warned the Democratic Party hasn't yet "renounced their crazy" on Thursday and that it could spell trouble for the party in 2028, but maintained that Republicans were likely to lose control of Congress in November.

During an interview on "The Chris Cuomo Project," host Chris Cuomo asked Maher if President Donald Trump and Republicans taking a "beating" in the midterm elections would mean the Democratic Party successfully made the case to the American people. 

"Absolutely not," Maher said. "They have not renounced their crazy at all. In fact, they're going full steam ahead. That's why I'm so worried about 2028. And a lot of the far left will take Trump's loss, they will misinterpret it as a recommendation for what they're trying to do. You know, the whole thing with communism — and it is communism."

"I know Trump says it, that doesn't mean it's wrong," he continued. "When you talk about taking over the means of production and taking over all the private industries, that's communism, folks. You can look it up."

BILL MAHER ADMITS HE COULD VOTE FOR JD VANCE, WARNS 'COWARDLY' DEMOCRATS FACE SOCIALIST TAKEOVER

"All this stuff, the Democrats could put this to the side for this election, even though they will be having these sort of internal debates," Maher added. "But you see that the sane wing of the party is very circumspect at how much they criticize this because they know there's just so much energy on that side."

"I mean, it's interesting we're talking about this on October 7, you know, which, man, they can't even give them the one day, you know?" he said. "It's just like that the Israeli craziness. That's another place the Democrats will see. We'll see if they can check themselves on that."

Maher said the midterm elections would be primarily about Trump.

"It is drunk on power," he said. "You know, it happens to both sides. They get in and just job one is just undoing the thing that the other a--hole did."  

"I mean, we always have battles, of course, both parties," Maher continued. "And we should. That's our system. But when it gets to be this vitriolic, this personal, this hateful, this just everything you do, I just want to undo it and disavow it, and even when it makes sense not to. They just hate. When hate takes over, people stop listening to any of the logic."

BILL MAHER BLASTS DEMOCRATIC PARTY, SAYS IT IS FINE WITH RELIGION 'AS LONG AS THAT FAITH ISN’T JEWISH'

Y. David Scharf, chair of Government Strategies & Controversies at Morrison and Cohen, agreed with Maher in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"Bill Maher is right to sound the alarm," he said. "What was once the far-left fringe of the Democratic Party is increasingly becoming its mainstream. That may win you elections in deep-blue states and congressional districts, but what plays in Brooklyn doesn't necessarily play in battleground America."

"Israel is the clearest example," Scharf continued. "When activists can't even put their hostility toward Israel aside on October 7, the anniversary of the deadliest day for Jews since the Holocaust, and party leaders are too afraid to call them out, you have to ask who's really running the show."

"Democrats may think they're building momentum for 2028," he added. "But there's a big difference between winning over your base and winning over America."

SHOCKING PERCENTAGE OF DEMOCRATS IDENTIFY AS 'DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS' ACCORDING TO NEW POLL: 'TOXIC POLICIES'

Maher said during an interview on CNN's "Fareed Zakaria GPS" that Republicans would suffer a "classic historical a-- whooping" in the November midterm elections.

The comedian argued that voters would use the midterms to punish Trump and Republicans before turning their attention to divisions within the Democratic Party ahead of the next presidential election.

"It’s going to be a classic historical a-- whooping," he said. "Now, 2028 is a different story. The Democrats have a crazy animal living in their house called the DSA, and they believe truly insane things. And they’re the energy of the party, and they’re going to make Gaza a genocide, a litmus test, and a lot of other really stupid stuff."

Fox News' CJ Womack contributed to this report.

item.title: Ex-NHLer Viktor Stalberg tells wild story about being traded in Russia — then not — by legendary coach
item.description: Viktor Stalberg reveals how Bob Hartley wanted him gone from Avangard Omsk, but the KHL club's owner stepped in with a blunt override of the coach.
item.content:encoded:
The sports world is full of stories about players who almost got traded, but you don't hear many like the one ex-NHLer Viktor Stalberg experienced during a stint in Russia's Kontinental Hockey League, which also involved a legendary tough coach.

Wait ... a strange story from the KHL? What?!

Stalberg spent eight seasons in the NHL and won a Stanley Cup with the 2013 Chicago Blackhawks, and while his last games in the league were with Ottawa in the 2016-17 season, he continued to be a high-level player in European leagues.

Eventually, he signed with KHL club Avangard Omsk, which, at the time, was coached by Bob Hartley, best known for winning a Stanley Cup with the 2000-01 Colorado Avalanche on top of being a very tough coach.

"I had a lot of interesting experiences," Stalberg said of his time in the KHL during a video interview to promote sportsbook Ozoon. "I also had Bob Hartley as a coach there, which I'm sure you've heard stories about. He's a brilliant hockey mind, but he might not be the easiest to handle. When I was there, we did not maybe click at first."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

He said that it became clear that he was not one of Hartley's favorite players on the team, and he was told by his agent that he was going to get waived by the team.

But it didn't happen, and he was told his status with the team was safe.

"My agent calls me again," Stalberg recalled. "'Hey, Bob really hates you. He does not want to play you or anything else this year.' That this is the deal. Like, 'He's gonna just bag-skate you for the rest of the year, right?'"

So, Stalberg asked for a trade, despite having a no-trade clause, and the team cut a deal with the then-Shanghai-based club Kunlun Red Star.

"I call the GM [in Shanghai]. I talk to the coach; I'm discussing where I'm playing on the power play next game."

However, after packing his bags and going to the rink, no one at Omsk said anything to him about this trade.

"So I'm like, what is going on here? Like I'm traded, right? Like nobody says anything.

"I go home, nobody calls," Stalberg said. "I'm like, 'Where's my flight, what is going on?' So then my agent again calls me back like a few hours later. He's like, 'Yeah, the owner told Bob to f--- off; you're staying."

Well, so much for that trade.

"So pretty much within, you know, in a week's time, my wife thought I was crazy," he laughed. "You know, like, 'I'm getting fired tomorrow. No, no, I'm staying. I'm getting traded to China tomorrow. No, no, I'm staying.' So it was a crazy few weeks there, but it ended up great."

Stalberg ultimately won Hartley, and he even wanted him to stick around the following season, but he wound up signing to play for Switzerland's Fribourg-Gotteron HC.
